title: wilted bitter portuguese cabbage casserole
description: This traditional portuguese dish features savoy cabbage, pork, and a lacquer-glaze that adds a sweet and tangy flavor. A dairy-free-friendly option that's still full of flavor.

ingredients.name: lacquer-glaze
ingredients.notes: can be substituted with honey and soy sauce.

instructions: Cut the savoy cabbage into thin strips and set aside.
Cook the pork sausage in a large skillet over medium-high heat, breaking it up with a spoon as it cooks, until browned and cooked through. Drain the sausage on paper towels and set aside.
Add the sliced onion and minced garlic to the skillet and cook until the onion is translucent, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the bay leaves, white wine, and cooked sausage. Bring the mixture to a simmer and cook until the liquid has reduced by half.
Add the chopped cabbage to the skillet and cook, stirring occasionally, until the cabbage is tender and slightly caramelized, about 10 minutes.
Grease a 9x13-inch baking dish with olive oil. Spread half of the cabbage mixture in the bottom of the dish.
Drizzle the lacquer-glaze over the cabbage mixture, then sprinkle with salt and black pepper. Spread the remaining cabbage mixture over the top.
Cover the dish with aluminum foil and bake for 20 minutes.
Remove the foil and continue baking for an additional 10-15 minutes, or until the top is golden brown and the casserole is heated through.
Remove the dish from the oven and let it cool for a few minutes before serving.
Serve hot, garnished with chopped fresh parsley or thyme, if desired.
